summary: The Dominican Republic admits tourists from countries including the US, Canada and the UK visa-free for 30 days (for longer stays the Dirección General de Migración grants an extension it describes as extendable up to 120 days), requires every traveler to complete the free digital e-Ticket form for both arrival and departure, and lets anyone holding a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen multiple-entry visa or permanent residence enter for tourism with a valid passport and a tourist card.

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including anyone who spent more than 12 hours in transit through such a country's airport. The list of origin countries the requirement applies to is the Dominican Republic's own and differs from WHO's risk list.

onwardTicket.text: The UK government says you may be refused entry if you do not have proof of onward or return travel when you arrive in the country. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket. No Dominican government page we could read states the rule.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read publishes a minimum amount. Canada's travel advice says you may need to prove adequate funds for the duration of your stay when you enter, and give the address where you will be staying.

declarations.name: e-Ticket (digital entry and exit form)
declarations.submitWindow: Online, for arrival and again for departure
declarations.text: Every passenger entering or leaving the Dominican Republic must complete the digital e-Ticket, a form required by the Dirección General de Migración and the Dirección General de Aduanas. The Dirección General de Migración says the e-Ticket is free and that unofficial lookalike sites charge for it, so use only the official eticket.migracion.gob.do site. The e-Ticket portal cites Laws 285-04, 115-17, 72-02 and 226-06, says the Ministry of Public Health also requires the form, and says the Unique Customs Declaration part is required only for adults (18 and over).

source.name: Dirección General de Migración — E-TICKET, ticket electrónico de entrada y salida

alsoStatedOn.name: Dirección General de Migración — e-Ticket portal (laws 285-04, 115-17, 72-02 and 226-06; Ministry of Public Health; Unique Customs Declaration for adults 18+)

currencyLimits.text: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent in Dominican pesos or another currency) and bearer instruments must be declared to customs officers on entry or exit, using the form provided for that purpose, with documents showing that the money was lawfully obtained.

source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas — Manual del Viajero (traveller's guide)

safety.text: The UK government describes the crime rate as high, from bag-snatching and pickpocketing to violent crime and carjacking. It says thieves on motorcycles snatch bags from pedestrians and reach into cars stopped at red lights, and that assaults on foreigners have occurred, including at beach resorts. It advises avoiding remote areas, particularly after dark, and not wearing expensive jewellery or carrying large amounts of cash.

tips.text: The e-Ticket entry and exit form is free at eticket.migracion.gob.do; the Dirección General de Migración says lookalike websites charge for it.

The UK government says motorbike taxis (motoconchos) are often driven badly and do not always provide passengers with a helmet, and advises using an authorised airport or hotel taxi service or booking from a registered provider.
The UK government says the Caribbean hurricane season normally runs from June to November.

faq.question: What is the Dominican Republic e-Ticket and who needs it?
faq.answer: The e-Ticket is a free, mandatory digital form required by the Dirección General de Migración and the Dirección General de Aduanas. Every passenger entering or leaving the country must complete it, at the official site eticket.migracion.gob.do; Migration says lookalike sites charge for it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: No. US citizens enter visa-free as tourists for 30 days; when you arrive by air, the tourist card is included in your airline ticket, according to the Government of Canada. You need a valid passport and the free e-Ticket form. The UK government tells British nationals they can pay to extend a visit up to 120 days.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 30 days in the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: Yes. The Dirección General de Migración says foreigners who want to stay longer than the 30 days set for tourists can apply online for a stay extension (prórroga), which it describes as extendable up to 120 days. The Government of Canada says to apply after you arrive and before your tourist card expires, and that overstaying can lead to deportation or refusal of re-entry.

faq.question: Do I still need to buy a tourist card for the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says that if you arrive by air, the cost of the tourist card is included in your airline ticket, and that if you arrive by sea you obtain the card at the point of entry from the Dirección General de Impuestos Internos. It says the e-Ticket does not replace the tourist card.

faq.question: Can I enter the Dominican Republic with a US, UK or Schengen visa instead of a Dominican visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Decree No. 691-07, foreigners who hold permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, the European Union (Schengen), Canada or Great Britain can enter for tourism with just a valid passport and a tourist card.
